recipes.name: Souvlaki
ingredients_raw: 3 pounds pork tenderloin, cut into 1 inch cubes
2 medium yellow onions, cut into 1 inch pieces
2 medium green bell peppers, cut into 1 inch pieces

steps.text: Mix oil, soy sauce, lemon juice, garlic, and oregano together in a large glass bowl.
Add pork, onions, and bell peppers, and stir until coated. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove pork and vegetables from marinade and shake off excess; thread onto skewers. Discard remaining marinade.

Cook on the preheated grill, turning frequently, until pork is no longer pink in the middle, 10 to 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Souvlaki
raw_recipe.description: Delicious souvlaki skewers made with marinated pork, onions, and bell peppers cooked on a grill until succulent, tender, and full of Greek flavor.

review.reviewBody:
Excellent.I served it with my own recipe for tzatziki sauce...
1/2 container sour cream
1/4 cucumber, shredded and drained
3 cloves garlic, shredded
1 teaspoon dill weed
salt to taste
Mix, then let sit for an hour and then mix again...very garlicy and yummy...I used it on everything (hamburgers as a topping, dipping sauce, wraps, etc) You will ove it!

As luck would have it, my grill ran out of gas right when I was about to prepare this dish. So, a lucky accident occurred thats worth another try! 
I dumped the entire thing, marinade and all, into a deep, stainless saute pan and sauted everything. I lidded the mixture for the first 3/4 of the cooking time (to ensure that the meat was cooked and the veggies soft). Following this, I increased the heat and removed the lid, thus boiling and thickening the remaining juices. The result was delicious! What was originally the marinade became a thick delicious sauce. The pork was ridiculously tender, and the greek flavor was prevalent throughout. 
The only thing I will be careful about next time is saltiness. I added the soy, as directed, but then also seasoned the dish and mine came out just a bit too salty.

Man did this turn out authentic, just like in our favorite Greek restaurants. I made two minor changes (sorry, I hate when people make big changed. These are small.). I added just a splash of white wine vinegar because I taste that in all the shish kebobs in Greek places. Two, I don't like my veggies crispy like most kebobs. I precut them and micro waved for 1.5 minutes just to soften them up. Then I marinated them and they soaked up the marinade much more. I used pork tenderloin which works very well with kebobs because it's hard to overcook. Once you see the edges browned to your liking, take them out and they are done. I served this with two other recipes on this site; baked Greek Style Lemon Potatoes and Spanakorizo (rice and spinach). Wow. Everything turned out near perfect, a rarity. Can't wait to try it with chicken thighs or tenderloin. So easy and delicious.

I made this and it turned out delicious! My husband said it was the best meal I had made yet. I did not kabob it. I cut everything up and put in on a baking sheet and cooked it on convection bake in my oven.
It cooked tender and juicy and got nice and browned. 
I baked some pita pockets and filled them with the ingredients and topped with homemade tatziki sauce. I also did not use but a few dashes of soy and not what the recipe called for. The soy is way to overwhelming if you use much more than a dash.

Grilling Perfection!This recipe is fun and easy to make. Skewers with like-size pieces of pork, onion and peppers cook evenly and therefore is easier to judge the grill time.I oiled the grill prior to cooking to reduce the food sticking and ease the ability to rotate the skewers frequently.The pork and vegetables did have a lovely grill flavor and crispiness that made it a pleasure to eat, while maintaining tenderness and juiciness.I served this Souvlaki dish with Near East Rice and it was the perfect light and flavorful meal. I used red and yellow peppers for color and more mild flavor than green peppers.

Wonderful!! I did make a few changes. For the sake of time I wanted to cook in the slow cooker. I put 2 pork tenderlions (about total 3 lbs) in the slow cooker with the marinade the night before and cooked it on low for 4 hours and 50 mins. It was tender and had great taste. I also used less sodium soy sauce. I served with some Tzatziki sauce and it was fantastic!

This was fantastic! Very easy and flavorful. I used a 2 lb. pork loin cut up and marinated for 2 hours, threw in a casserole dish and baked for 25 minutes at 400 degrees. I served with rice, pita, a cucumber dill sauce and pita bread. My 2 and 3 year old kids even ate it. A keeper!

Easy, and entire picky family loved it. I'd use JLambert sauce suggestion for spread...with modification the pork already has garlic...sauce completes this great dish... 1/2 container of sour cream, 1/2 cucumber finely chopped, teaspoon of dill or less depending on your fam. preference. Coat inside of pita with the sauce, layer spinach at the bottom, then add pork and green and red pepper then a dlop of yum sauce...on fam. Calendar rotation, thank you
Ps don't over grill the pork leave slightly pink in side.

was very good. I marinaded the chicken for 8 hrs. We unfortunately couldn't grill them so I made them on the stove. My daughter wanted to eat this with rice so I made extra marinade to pour on top of the rice w. the tzatziki sauce.
An absolute hit with the whole family. Doubled ingredients for 5-1/2 lbs of pork tenderloin and added red, yellow and orange bell peppers and baked in oven at 350 for 40 minutes. Everyone loved it!

EXCELLENT!! I made ours with chicken. I marinaded the chicken and onions together then, as others, put mine in roasting pan and baked for 10 min at 400. Added in the peppers and zucchini (subbed for green pepper) and mixed together...five more minutes in oven then under the grill for 10 to give it a char. Chicken moist and veggies were al dente. DIVINE! Served with Greek style potatoes by Cathie from this site...also excellent.
So good

I made this exactly as the recipe called for, except I used gluten-free soy sauce for my gluten-sensitive kid, plus a skewer with tofu for my vegetarian kid. We all loved it! Definitely going into the regular rotation.
I followed the recipe exactly as it was my first time out. Perfect
Too cold to grill, so I made this into a bowl. Served over rice. The marinade made the pork very tender and flavorful! Also added mushrooms
Easy and super delicious. Made 3x in 2 weeks. Serve with the cucumber tzatziki sauce for omg yumminess.
It's traditionally made with lamb. All the rest are alternatives.
Has the taste I was looking for !
The Lamb is incredible! Great friendly staff… will return! Also, the Baklava is amazing!!!
Wow!!!! Loved this. I did make a few changes, used boneless skinless chicken thighs, added a splash of white wine vinegar and used a bit less oil.
